interactions.flavorLineOne: Your clan's reputation grows, and with it your rewards.

Represent your clan well, Guardian.

This banner will grow in strength as your clan demonstrates its power.
For a split second, it seemed like Louis was staring at you. Hawthorne didn't seem to notice. She accepts the gift on his behalf.
Hawthorne is impressed by your dedication to bringing more Guardians into the fold, and she offers a reward in return.

"Love letters? The latest Omolon catalogue? Criminal activity? Whatever it is, you're real popular these days, Guardian."

Hawthorne flips a hawk-nibbled envelope over to you. The letter inside reads,

"To the Hero of the City,

"Curiouser and curiouser! A whole Salvation gang absconding with a Ketch, and a Golden Age AI locked up on a station alone… well, that's news plenty would pay for. A BrayTech AI is a valuable thing, no matter how poor her personal attitude. We'd better make sure she doesn't fall into the wrong hands.

"While you were clearing the nest, I had my people doing some digging on the side. Their key discovery was that many mysteries still wait in Europa's orbit. More investigation means more profit, and an answer to some lingering questions, eh?

"My last contract with a Lightbearer ended… unhappily, let's say. But I believe ours will be a fruitful partnership.

"As ever, your friend, the Spider."

Return to the "Vesper's Host" dungeon and uncover its secrets.

Hawthorne raises her eyebrows at you. "Your correspondent has graduated from letters to packages. I'm telling you, Guardian, you're putting Kadi out of business like this."

You tear open the latest envelope from Spider and a data chip falls out. The attached message reads,

"Dear Guardian,

"We've learned so much together, haven't we? I treat my partners well. Look at how high my last partner has risen in City authority. Always remember what Spider can do for you.

"Now, for Vesper Station… There's an ultimate control mechanism. Bray's personal key. And if you control the AI, you control the station. Vesper Central seems lonely up there. A bit out of control. I think you'll agree she could use a guiding hand.

"My agents have turned up one little key on their search for the big one. You take it and you grab what you want, and you remember it was your old chum who had you in his thoughts this whole time.

"XOXO, etc, the Spider."

PERMISSIONS GRANTED:
TechAccess|Storage|Restricted|42

"A mind heist?" Hawthorne says with a laugh, shaking her head. "Only you, Guardian. Only you."

She turns to look out over the City for a moment, then up to the sky. "I'm glad you helped Eris out, but Ikora found out about everything. You can't keep much from her Hidden. I hear she's authorizing future dives into the Mindscape…"

Hawthorne turns back to you. "Hopefully, Eris got what she was looking for. Because it sounds like you two opened a door that should have stayed closed."

"No one will tell me what happened down there," Hawthorne says with a nervous look back at Ikora. "Whenever I ask, she says it's 'privileged information' and shuts me down."

Anxiously looking around, Hawthorne shakes her head. "I won't ask you to go against Ikora's wishes. She's gotta be keeping secrets for a good reason. But I haven't seen her that shaken since she learned about Savathûn having the Light…"

Hawthorne furrows her brow and stares into the distance for a moment. "Actually… maybe it's better if I don't know, " she murmurs, shifting her attention back to you. "Sometimes the truth is more terrifying than your own imagination."

Hawthorne holds the latest envelope back for a moment.

"Either give your mystery admirer your comm frequency or a restraining order, but stop using my place as a dead drop, yeah?"

You nod, contrite. Hawthorne passes you the letter, watched by a fierce Louis. It reads,

"To the Guardian, my friend and partner in perfectly legal enterprise,

"A job well done as usual! That's what I like to see in a partner. Steadiness. Trustworthiness, even. And a willingness to share the profits. That little AI up there is lonely, don't you think? Best keep an eye on her. We haven't turned up that key yet, but it's got to exist. One access code implies another. That's what I think. And I'm not often wrong!

"All perfectly aboveboard, of course. It would be a kindness, even—I'm sure she could use the distraction.

"With all the usual sickening sentiments, the Spider."

Mysteries linger within Vesper Station, and in Spider's intentions for Vesper Central.
"Feeling ambitious this week, weren't you? Well done, Guardian." —Hawthorne

Hawthorne turns to you with a serious look in her eyes. She passes a datapad to you containing schematics of the Leviathan and transmat beacon details for the Leviathan's Tribute Hall.

"Eris is up to something," Hawthorne says with a tightness in her voice. "She won't say what, and she asked me to relay this to you, personally, ignoring Vanguard protocol."

She continues with a sigh. "I don't like going around Ikora, but whatever this is… it sounds urgent. I don't know Eris well, but I trust her judgment. If we have to break protocol to get something done, so be it. You should go see what this is all about."

Launch the "Duality" dungeon from the Moon in the Director.

Hawthorne nods at your approach. "Guardian. Ever thought about getting an apartment down in the City? Something with a balcony, maybe a mailbox? I found this under my door this morning. Nearly slipped on your mail—and Louis nearly did worse to it."

With an apologetic grimace, you open the letter. It reads:

"To my dearest scallywag,

"I've got a job for you, and it comes with a sob story. I had an agent investigating an orbital station above Europa for salvage. She lost contact. It'd have to be something worse than Salvation vagrants knocking around up there to take her down. All we're getting on the Europa channels now are automated warnings. Old Human ones. I'm not sending anyone else on my payroll after a corpse. It's time for drastic measures—and you, Guardian, are the most drastic measure I can think of.

"The pay's good: whatever you can salvage. A Golden Age station is a treasure hoard for a canny explorer. I'll content myself with your leftovers.

"Give it a look. Just try not to crash this station, too, would you?

"With anticipation, your friend, the Spider."

Hawthorne hurries to hand you a datapad. "This just came in from a communications relay on Titan. The commander asked me to deliver it to you immediately."

The datapad contains coordinates on Titan for the New Pacific Arcology. "The Hive have a foothold there, but the deputy commander says the situation has changed," Hawthorne says with concern.

"Something about a Lucent Hive ship entering Titan's atmosphere and diving into the ocean," Hawthorne says and motions to the datapad. "Details look scarce. But whatever's going on can't be good."

Launch the "Ghosts of the Deep" dungeon from the H.E.L.M. in the Director.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"I'm glad you were able to rescue Bean, he's going to be a great asset to healing the Traveler," Micah says with relief.

"I can't help but be worried about what you found while searching for him. I thought the Psion defectors sided with the Witness…" She falls silent in thought. "But it's looking more and more like that may be a deception."

Micah lowers her voice in suspicion. "There's something else going on here. Something we're going to have to tackle head-on in the future, if we're lucky."

Micah has telemetry on another unpartnered Ghost. "Your next target is Link, a member of a covert team of unpartnered Ghosts called the Watchful Eye."

With worry in her voice she explains, "His last known location was roughly in the area of the Ocean of Storms on the Moon. But he may have moved on by now."

Go to the Moon and pick up Link's trail.

"Some Ghosts have searched for centuries for their Guardian. I know yours did," Micah-10 says with an unseen smile in her voice. 

"The unpartnered Ghost Dejana was last seen in the EDZ investigating Taken activity. Hopefully we can find her quick."

"Come back in one piece, okay?"

"So I found telemetry for Bean." There's a hint of mirth in Micah's tone. "He's a handful, always rushing off into hostile territory. He and I tend to cross paths on remote scouting missions, so the fact that his beacon pinged from Nessus shouldn't surprise me."

For a moment, Micah is quiet. Then, fondly, she says, "But that's what I like about him. No fear, no hesitation. Bean just plows through. We need that kind of energy here."

"Go make sure he didn't get caught in a temporal loop or some other Vex nonsense," Micah says with a laugh. "I'll keep an eye on things here."

"Welcome back, I've got another Ghost telemetry for you." Micah is eager to get to work. "This time, it's Akasha. She's an unpartnered Ghost that has been systematically scanning Awoken territory for years."

Micah brings up a map of the Dreaming City on the display. "I got a lock on her beacon in the Dreaming City, probably still trying to find her Guardian. I need you to head out and find Akasha and bring her back safe and sound."

"I look forward to your return."

"Mars." Micah says it like a curse. "Of course Citrine would be on Mars."

There's a mixture of wryness and frustration in Micah's voice. "She's been obsessed with Warmind hardware for a long time. I don't know how many times Ana had to tell her she wasn't going to build her a combat frame to ride in. Just so she could 'have arms to beat a Hive with.'"

All humor aside, Micah gets down to business. "Citrine means well, but we need her here. Be careful out there, Guardian. "

"I have Ghost telemetry for you, but a word of warning on this one." Micah sighs. "Anwar is a Ghost who has been through a lot. He was once a close confidant of the Speaker. After the Speaker died, Anwar started to question his connection to the Light, and began to seek the truth about Darkness."

"Anwar believes the Darkness is an intrinsic, universal force that must be tended to like a garden, lest it grow unruly. Do not let Anwar's beliefs cast a shadow of doubt on his allegiances. He is an unwavering ally, but one who questions everything."

"His telemetry data leads me to believe he may be inside the Pyramid on Europa," Micah says with a wary tone. "I don't know what you'll find there. Be safe, Guardian."

"I found the general location of Heilung. She's another member of the Watchful Eye," Micah explains, short and to the point.

"Turns out, Heilung was sent on a long-term recon operation inside Savathûn's throne world," she admits with some surprise. "But that was over a year ago. There's been no contact with Heilung since, and I don't know what to expect. The Hidden provided me with her last known coordinates.
We'll have to start there and see what we can find."

"Guardian, I have telemetric data for the Ghost Balthazar." Micah is eager to get to work. "He's an old friend of Peach, the first Ghost you recruited."

With seriousness, she adds, "Balthazar is a scholar like Anwar, but usually not as daring in field work. Which makes my discovery of his telemetric data on the moon all the more concerning."

"If Balthazar has gone to the moon he must have good reason, but we need him here. We need every ghost we can find." Micah says with urgency. There is little time left.

"Please, bring him back, and make sure he's safe."

"I've been observing the energy coming from the Traveler, and… it's not good." Micah can't hide her worry. 

"While we've been doing everything we can to heal the Traveler, the Witness's push to complete the final shape hasn't slowed."

"I'm sending you to find Hecate, a scholar in Hive lore who once studied under Toland, the Shattered and Eris Morn," Micah explains. "Hecate was investigating a rumor that members of House Dusk were trying to ally with Hive broods in the Cosmodrome. The House of Devils have been gone for a long time, though. There has to be something else going on." 

"Good hunting, Guardian."

"Talk about addressing the source of a problem directly, huh?" Micah says. There's nothing quite like uprooting a weed. "Good job. You and I both know the work's never done… but I think you can take a moment to feel proud."

If the surroundings are any judge, the Traveler is also feeling better. Some things might not be mendable, but it's clear that having ended the Witness entirely has made a huge difference. However the Traveler heals and grows in the future, this one great thorn has been plucked out.

Micah says she's going to be sticking around in the Pale Heart—to learn, to help, to grow for herself. She's come to understand some new things while she's been here and is looking forward to more. She might not be right here all the time, but that's the nature of a Hunter, after all.

"See you around, Guardian," she says. "The Six Coyotes know your name."
The Arbor of Light extends its gratitude to you.

"Peach was lucky to get out of that situation with only a few dents and dings." Micah's relief is tempered by uncertainty. "The world outside of the Pale Heart is transforming… We've got no room for error now. I'll get Peach set up in a cleansing team here in the Pale Heart." 

"I'll contact you when I have telemetry on another Ghost. Stay safe, Guardian."

This quest reward can only be accepted on one character, but armor is unlocked for all three classes when this quest is completed.

Return to Ghost in the Pale Heart to decrypt or focus engrams on another class.

"The final shape spreading to the moon isn't a surprise. But that it's hitting the Hive as hard as anyone else?" Micah sighs. "I guess there really is nowhere safe. No promise or allegiance that can save you."

"But ah, one thing at a time, I guess. I'll let you know when I know more."

"The final shape has reached Earth." Micah is weary. "We're running out of time."

With a sigh, Micah continues. "I knew we might reach this point eventually, but seeing it is something else entirely. But we're not ready to move against the Witness. The Traveler isn't ready. Though… we may not have time. But we only get one shot at defeating the Witness. We have to make it our best."

This quest reward can only be accepted on one character, but armor is unlocked for all three classes when this quest is completed.

"We've got a lot to do before we can strike at the Witness." Micah-10 is eager to add to the combined efforts of the coalition.

"I think it'll be the smaller, more humble kind of reinforcement that wins the day," she adds, recruiting you to track down unpartnered Ghosts that can help treat the wounds of the Traveler.

Your first target is Peach, a wayward Ghost last seen in the Cosmodrome on Earth. Track Peach down and bring her home.

"So this is interesting…" Micah trails off for a moment as she reads your report. "Akasha returned some analytics from her scans of the Dreaming City's Ley Lines, and it's troubling. There's Hive activity surging through the Ascendant Plane. Xivu Arath's brood. And as far as I can tell, she's a no-show here."

A thought crosses Micah's mind. "Which means she's cut her losses from the Witness. But that also means she's planning something else…"

"If we make it out of this alive, I've got a bad feeling there'll be another war waiting for us on the horizon. Nothing we can do about that right now, though," she notes with a hint of resignation. 

"Get back out there. One apocalypse at a time."

This quest reward can be accepted on only one character, but armor is unlocked for all three classes when this quest is completed.

"Citrine is so sweet. She profusely apologized for her delay in arrival… and tried to hide the fact that she was stripping the Warmind bunker for parts," Micah says with a laugh.

"I'm putting her with a patrol of Ghosts to help expunge the Witness's corruption and she's taken right to it. And with any luck, she'll put her analytical mind to expediting the process."


"Good work out there, Guardian. I'll let you know when I find another Ghost."

"I've… never told anyone this, but I knew Cayde. Before he was a Guardian. Before I was a Guardian," Micah confesses in a moment of grief over Anwar's death.

She speaks of their time together on Europa before the Collapse, and how she found out about this past by performing a Guardian taboo: researching her own past.

"Cayde doesn't remember. And… that's okay. What matters is that I'm here. That he's here. That somehow, in the face of all this loss and hopelessness… we found each other. I can hug him, one last time… and remind him that he was missed."

"That he saved me."

This quest reward can only be accepted on one character, but armor is unlocked for all three classes when this quest is completed.

Micah bristles with frustration. "If what Heilung has already told me is correct, Savathûn has aligned her brood against the Witness… but she's hedging her bets. She has some other plan in the works, something she intends to pursue after the Witness is defeated. She thinks its defeat is inevitable. I should be inspired by that vote of confidence, but coming from her? Nah."

"I'll let you know when I have more Ghost telemetry to follow up on, Guardian." Then, with a warmth in her voice she adds, "Great work out there."

"I know Anwar's death weighs heavily on Balthazar," Micah explains. "He will heal, in time, as the Traveler will. Perhaps in their shared healing, Balthazar will find new spiritual connections to the Traveler too."

There is relief in Micah's voice. "Thank you, Guardian. As soon as I've pinned down another Ghost's location, I'll contact you."

This quest reward can only be accepted on one character, but armor is unlocked for all three classes when this quest is completed.

"Hecate is back with us, and not a moment too soon," Micah says, tension evident in her voice. The end is approaching.

"The Vanguard are rallying our forces together for the final push. I've sent Hecate out to aid with healing the Traveler, but… there's not much time left. I can feel the tension escalating to a breaking point. I can feel the universe cracking under the strain." Micah grows silent.

"The final shape is upon us, and I can only pray that we've done enough to fight back against it." For a moment, that feels like the end. But then, with a hint of hope in her voice, Micah offers one final benediction:

"Eyes up, Guardian."

The console has been hastily, but cleverly, rigged for communications. When you approach, it flickers to life.

Micah-10 tells you about her mission to find and save unpartnered Ghosts. They returned to help the Traveler as soon as they could, but the Witness's infection caused chaos. They need help.

The console's interface shows an area of the Pale Heart that Micah has marked. She says she's receiving telemetry from a Ghost in the area, but it must be damaged; the signal is unclear. You'll need to search to find it.

She also says that some of the Ghosts have helped scout safe zones within the Pale Heart. You should be able to use them as LZs to travel more efficiently.

The fissure of Light brightens slightly in response to the Ghost's presence. Motes of Light well up and drift toward the damaged Ghost you carry, like dandelion seeds floating in the wind. Micah's machinery whirrs into high gear, analyzing what it can of the patterns in the Traveler's Light.

However, the damaged Ghost looks far from healed…

The Light from the Traveler surrounds you, and something seems different when you bring the damaged Ghost to the fissure of Light. 

Even this may not be enough. However, this time when you examine the Ghost, you see something more: echoes of a corrupting touch, silhouetted against the Traveler's Light. Perhaps this is the true nature of the injury.

"Guardian," Micah says when the feed opens again. "I can tell already something has changed for the better. I'm processing the readings now. Give me a moment, but early prognosis is very, very hopeful." 

It's taken hard work to get to this point, and there's a note of tangible relief in her voice as she talks. Relief for her charge, and for what it may mean for the future. "Thank you," she says. "Let's keep it up."

"Good work as usual, Guardian," Micah says when you return. "I can already tell you've done as much as you can. At this point, it looks like we'll need to deal with the main act—the Witness—before we can make any more difference. Fixing holes only works for so long when the Witness is busy making new ones by the moment, you know." 

Her tone is somberly hopeful—much relies on the capability to defeat the Witness and drive it from the Traveler, but if that can be accomplished then the future will be bright.
A gift for your efforts.

"Hang on a moment," Micah says. "Oh darling, that's a huge data swap—" 

She takes a moment to sort through the information she's receiving from Differential Calculus, the healed Ghost. The data looks promisingly revelatory on a first analysis: the Traveler is hurt by what the Witness has done to it, and all of the lost Ghosts have been trying to help it, in their way—seeking out dangerous places to get closer to the Traveler. 

The instinct is sound. Revitalizing the connection between Ghost and Traveler helps both, although the scale of the Traveler is much greater than any single Ghost. There's still a long road ahead: if the Traveler even CAN be healed completely.

But there is a duty, held by Micah-10 and the Ghosts she shepherds, to do everything in their power to help. And they'd welcome your continuing assistance. "Keep up the good work," Micah-10 says. She has a bigger picture mission in mind: tackling the Witness's influence directly while she works to track other missing Ghosts.

"Nicely done, Guardian," Micah says. She's seen the effects of your efforts out in the Pale Heart, and she's impressed, optimistic for the future.

There's still more to be done. Micah mentions Ulan-Tan, a historical Warlock with theories about Light and Darkness which were considered dangerous at the time. All Light was part of itself, he had concluded: Ghosts connected to Guardians connected to the Traveler, inextricably tied together. Micah thinks—maybe—that the problem with this damaged Ghost is that they've been disconnected from the Traveler in some way and forced to rely only on their own Light.

She's found some places, deep in the Pale Heart, that she thinks are as close to the Traveler's unfiltered essence as you can possibly get. Maybe there you can join this Ghost's Light with the Traveler's again. And even if that doesn't help, you'll still know more than you did before.

"No harm, no foul," Micah says, though she'd clearly prefer the idea works. The slow process of eliminating what doesn't work isn't ideal for situations like these. "Sending you one of the locations I've dug up now."

"Good news, bad news," Micah says, clearly putting a brave face on things. It's a little of both. It would have been nice to find this lost Ghost in perfect condition, but at least they're alive.

The trouble is that it's difficult to know how to help. Simply exposing this Ghost to the Traveler's Light didn't seem to do anything immediately, but the Pale Heart is full of wonders. The line to Micah crackles as she hums in thought.

"Heal one, heal the other, maybe?" she says eventually. It's hard to miss that the Traveler's as hurt as this Ghost is, even if it's in a different way. The growth in the Arbor suggests you're on the right track, but not enough yet. Micah asks you to make a sweep around the Pale Heart, looking for things out of the ordinary—concentrations of Light that beg to be freed, or especially virulent servants of the Witness attacking vulnerable places.

It's just a hunch. But it's the best you've got, and this Ghost is counting on your help.
